newsitem.title: ITALY: Magistrates probe Italian leftist leader - Ansa.
newsitem.headline: Magistrates probe Italian leftist leader - Ansa.

text.p: Rome magistrates are investigating Massimo D'Alema, head of the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), in connection with alleged illegal party funding, the Italian news agency Ansa reported on Monday.

The agency, citing unnamed sources, said D'Alema's name was on a preliminary list of people to be investigated about a property deal in 1994. Two company officials and two PDS executives were also on the list, it said.

The investigation involves the sale of a building by a Rome company to a company controlled by a cooperative group that was traditionally close to the PDS and its predecessor, the Italian Communist Party, Ansa said.
Magistrates suspect that money from the deal may have wound up in the coffers of the PDS, it said.
D'Alema's lawyer said in a statement the deal involved no wrongdoing. It was registered and involved a mortgage to the party, he said.
A magistrates' preliminary list, known as the "register of investigated people," is supposed to remain confidential.
If enough evidence is found, it can be followed up by a "judicial notice" formally notifying a person that he is under investigation and should seek legal advice.
